newsitem.title: USA: State St chief repeats bank not for sale.
newsitem.headline: State St chief repeats bank not for sale.

text.p: State Street Boston Corp Chairman Marshall Carter said again on Tuesday that his bank is not for sale despite reports of recent overtures from Bank of New York.
"We are not for sale," Carter told reporters after a speech to the International Development Conference here.

Carter confirmed a report in last week's Wall Street Journal that he had met Bank of New York Chairman J. Carter Bacot to discuss possible joint ventures, but denied that the possibility of a merger was discussed.

Much consolidation has already occured in the custody market, where about 14 major players have been reduced to a half dozen in the past few years, Carter said. "It actually has already occurred," he said.
There is still room for the big players to gain market share, however, he added. "You basically have a market where the three major players (each) only have 10 percent market share," Carter said.
State Street, for example, is a custodian for about $2.7 trillion of assets out of about $35 trillion of total assets held worldwide, Carter said.
